en: Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 8.17. The Dyad on Taints and Things Subject to Taints (Āsavasāsavaduka)

Dependent on states that are both without taints (anāsava) and not without taints (na-anāsava), there arises a state that is both without taints and not without taints, by way of root condition (hetu-paccaya).
Dependent on states that are both without taints and not without taints, there arises a state that is not without taints and not [without] taints, by way of root condition.
Dependent on states that are both without taints and not without taints, there arises a state that is not without taints...
States that are neither-outflow nor outflow, as well as states that are both neither-outflow and outflow, arise with a root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both neither-outflow and outflow, a state that is neither-outflow and outflow arises with a root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both neither-outflow and outflow, a state that is neither-outflow... [arises].
A state that is neither with taints nor without taints arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither with taints nor without taints and a state that is without taints, states that are neither with taints nor without taints, as well as states that are neither with taints nor without taints and without taints, arise by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither with taints nor without taints and a state that is neither with taints nor without taints and without taints, [a state] that is neither with taints nor without taints... [arises].
A state that is neither *āsava* nor non-*āsava* arises by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is both neither *āsava* nor non-*āsava* and neither *āsava* nor non-*āsava*, a state that is neither *āsava* nor non-*āsava* arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is both neither *āsava* nor non-*āsava* and neither *āsava* nor non-*āsava*, a state that is neither *āsava* nor non-*āsava* arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both neither *āsava* nor non-*āsava* and neither *āsava* nor non-*āsava*, a state that is neither *āsava* nor non-*āsava* arises... [and so forth].
Diverse states, as well as both diverse and non-diverse outflows, arise by way of the root condition.

(Abbreviated. Nine in the case of the root; nine in the case of the object; ... [and so on] ... one in the case of resultant; ... [and so on] ... nine in the case of non-disappearance. (Full detail for all.)
